sentences.text: Halisaurus was an extinct genus of mosasaur that reached lengths of 3 to 4 meters.
This small creature possessed poorly differentiated flippers and lacked the hyperphalangy found in more advanced relatives.
The type specimen of H. arambourgi includes a disarticulated skull and 27 articulated vertebrae found near Khouribga in central Morocco.
The pterygoid bone of this species preserves twelve teeth, which is three more than found in the type species.
A BBC program suggested that Halisaurus hid in underwater caves to ambush small animals like Hesperornis.
The type species of the genus Halisaurus is H. platyspondylus, which was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1869.
Marsh renamed Halisaurus to Baptosaurus in 1870 because he thought the name was preoccupied by the fish Halosaurus.
Under modern rules, the name Baptosaurus is considered a junior synonym of Halisaurus because the names differ by only one letter.
In 2023, Shaker et al. named H. hebae based on fossils from the Late Cretaceous Dakhla Formation in Egypt.
H. auriculatus was described in 2026 by Shaker et al. based on specimen NVP040 from the Dakhla Formation.
Despite its small size, Halisaurus was likely a relatively poor swimmer compared to other small mosasaurs.
In 2005, Nathalie Bardet and colleagues described the new species Halisaurus arambourgi and reassigned H. sternbergii to the genus Eonatator.
A 2017 analysis by Tiago R. Simões and colleagues placed Halisaurus and the Halisaurinae as a sister group to the Mosasaurinae.
At least four species of Halisaurus are currently considered valid: H. platyspondylus, H. arambourgi, H. hebae, and H. auriculatus.
The species H. onchognathus is considered dubious because all known remains were destroyed during the Second World War.
The genus Halisaurus belongs to the subfamily Halisaurinae.
Known species of Halisaurus include H. platyspondylus, H. ortlebi, H. arambourgi, and the uncertain H. onchognathus.
Halisaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, spanning from the Santonian to the Danian, between 85.7 and 61.66 million years ago.
The genus appeared early in mosasaur evolution during the Santonian stage.
The type specimen of H. platyspondylus comes from the Maastrichtian-age New Egypt Formation in New Jersey.
H. platyspondylus ranged along the eastern coast of North America during the Middle to Late Maastrichtian.
H. arambourgi lived during the Late Maastrichtian and has been found in northern Africa and potentially the Middle East.
The exact phylogenetic position of Halisaurus within the mosasaur family tree has long been controversial.
Researchers suggest that H. ("Phosphorosaurus") ponpetelegans might represent a distinct genus requiring a new name rather than belonging to Halisaurus.
